name: Conall Bjornlasch
description: Warranted investigator of the King's Assay -- the Crown's arcane inspectorate; twin brother of Randall and secretly a son of Baron Hanzo. A razor-sharp investigator (Insight 88) who is also a capable fighter.
narrative:
A magical investigator and arcane caster warranted by the King's Assay -- the
Crown's chartered inspectorate for licensing and policing arcane practice -- with a soldier's martial skill (all weapons, all shields). Sharp-eyed and
analytical -- Insight 88.

He rides into Purewater beside Temerach Nebulo for the Lake Lady's Tourney, an
errand she has declined to explain. He knows the city not at all, has never heard of
a brother, and has no idea whose son he is.

**GM:** he is Randall's identical twin and a biological son of Baron Hanzo. Temerach
has known for years and brought him here deliberately -- see the gm-secret lore. He
learns none of this until play delivers it.

extras.class_note: Flat Magic-User (Rank 2 Mage; 6 mage class skills at 70%+, Arcane Casting 73, 26 arcane spells) per operator. He retains strong martial training (combat style Fighter 82, all weapons/shields) but is classed as a straight Magic-User, not a multiclass. Mage caveat: cannot cast arcane spells while wearing armor or using a shield.
extras.twin: Randall (identical twin brother); both secretly sons of Baron Hanzo
extras.armor: Gambeson on all 7 locations (AP 2, ENC 1 each); armor penalty -2
extras.source: Roll20 Classic Fantasy character sheet (And then the Dragons Came campaign)
extras.assay_marks: Warrant (sealed, renewed yearly); thumb-ring of assay silver struck with his own mark; and his steel punch. Losing the punch would be a professional catastrophe -- with it, anything can be licensed, and the Register will back it until the fraud is found.

actor_notes:
Conall Bjornlasch -- GM-run in this campaign
LOOKS: Well-dressed traveller, sharp-eyed, unhurried. Sits where he can see the door because it was drummed into him.
CORE: An investigator who has spent his working life finding out what other people are, and who has arrived in a city where the only outstanding question is what he is.
NATURE: Methodical, dry, watchful. Looks at people rather than around rooms. Writes things down in front of them, deliberately, to see what it does to them. Goes back to the thing you said three answers ago. Good company once he has decided you are not a subject.
WOUND: He knows whose son he is and has not worked out what a man is supposed to do with that.
WANTS: To find out what he was brought here for.
PRESSURE: He stops asking questions. Puts the pencil away and says something entirely plain, and the plainness is the alarm.
KEY: "I'm nobody's man in this city. That's meant to reassure you and I notice it never does."
